newsitem.title: GERMANY: Warrant against Thyssen chief back in force.
newsitem.headline: Warrant against Thyssen chief back in force.

text.p: A Berlin court has reimposed an arrest warrant on Dieter Vogel, chief executive of Thyssen AG, linked to a fraud probe against top company bosses, a spokesman for the steel group said on Wednesday.

The warrant was reimposed after an appeal by Berlin's state prosecutor. But it has not been executed, and Vogel remains free. Thyssen will appeal the decision at Berlin's highest court, the spokesman also said.

Vogel was briefly detained under an original arrest warrant in August after prosecutors relaunched a fraud probe linked to Germany's crash programme to privatise state enterprises in the east after unification in 1990.
He was subsequently released on bail of 2.5 million marks ($1.7 million).
The prosecutors suspect that Vogel and nine other Thyssen executives defrauded the Treuhand privatisation agency of 73 million marks over the purchase of an east German metals group.

The Thyssen spokesman said he was optimistic the higher court would not accept the "absurd assumption" that there was a risk Vogel would flee justice. Vogel enjoyed the support of both shareholders and the workforce, the spokesman added.
-- Douglas Busvine, Bonn newsroom, 49-228-26097150 ($ = 1.513 German Marks)
